observations: GitHub execution and Issue ownership verification succeeded on the public repository.
The real browser decrypted the challenge from github-actions[bot].
The owner submitted a 92-character authorization code through an encrypted Issue comment.
The worker matched exactly one code from the authenticated owner.
The terminal rendered new output but full plaintext code echo was absent.
The obsolete echo condition timed out after 10 seconds; no Enter or token publication occurred.
The encrypted error reached the browser; cleanup closed the Issue.

regression.fixtureChange: Use the observed prompt, synthetic OAuth parameter structure, and stars plus the final six input characters.
regression.beforeFix: The updated external-process fixture failed authorization scenarios against the old full-echo condition.
regression.afterFix: The existing worker acceptance scenarios pass and record masked echo mode without logging its suffix.

limitations: No real model turn or history encryption is tested here.
Only one authenticated GitHub actor participated; two-member concurrent use is not established.

The synthetic provider-error branch and decorative success wrapping are not literal captures of real failure/success frames; the success parser markers, token shape, and masking are empirically confirmed.

publicLogAudit.limitation: Pattern scanning supplements typed logging and encryption; it is not a proof against every possible disclosure.

browserEvidence.csp: Built launcher policy plus self connection only for the temporary local bootstrap endpoint.

sharedSecretConsumer.limitation: Official auth status verifies environment recognition, not an inference request or multi-user concurrency.

sharedSecretInference.limitation: One synthetic model turn using the existing shared Secret in a fresh VM. Does not establish browser/Morty chat, tool execution, personal history isolation, other member permissions, or concurrent account use.
